entities.summary: Quintus Tineius Sacerdos was a Roman senator who played a pivotal role in shaping the governance of Rome during the 2nd century CE. Attested as Consul Suffectus on March 16, 193, alongside Publius Julius Scapula Priscus, he exemplifies the importance of senatorial leadership in the Roman Republic's twilight years. His tenure as Consul Suffectus occurred during a period of significant political upheaval, as the Roman Empire faced internal strife and external threats from neighboring powers. The legacy of Quintus Tineius Sacerdos lies in his contribution to the Roman Senate's efforts to maintain stability and order in the face of these challenges. As a senator, he was deeply invested in the well-being of Rome and its people, working tirelessly to promote the interests of the state and its citizens. His commitment to public service and his dedication to the Roman Senate have left an indelible mark on the annals of Roman history, serving as a testament to the enduring power of senatorial leadership in the face of adversity. Quintus Tineius Sacerdos' remarkable story is a powerful reminder of the importance of civic duty and the need for effective leadership in times of crisis. Through his service, he helped to shape the course of Roman history, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continues to inspire and educate scholars and historians today.
